_doc: Camera-position statements for the Q16 photographs: what each source literally says about where the camera stood or which way it looked. Built by build_statements.py; every quote was found in the saved source text. tier documented = the source says it (it is a statement, not a coordinate); tier lead = a statement the source takes from a book that may not be used (Frassanito), listed so that nothing is hidden. No source read gives a coordinate.

statements.quote: View taken from Cemetery Hill at about position of right gun of Wiedrich's (i. e. Weidrich's) Battery
statements.says: camera on Cemetery Hill at about the position of the right gun of Wiedrich's Battery (title from item); no direction given in the title
statements.note: The record's summary adds the German Reformed Church in the background and cites Frassanito: that part is not used (lead only).

statements.quote: The lunettes in the foreground covered guns of Stewarts (B, 4th U.S. Artillery) Battery.
statements.says: the earthwork lunettes in the foreground of the 'cemetery gate' view covered guns of Stewart's battery (caption continues; Gardner's Sketch Book no. 39)

statements.quote: The road on the left is the Baltimore pike.
statements.says: in the view of Gettysburg from Cemetery Hill the Baltimore Pike is the road on the left (Gardner's Sketch Book plate 35 caption as transcribed by LOC)

statements.quote: Road on right is the Chambersburg pike. Embankment in centre is unfinished railroad. Large building on left is Pennsylvania College.
statements.says: view of Gettysburg from the northwest: Chambersburg Pike on the right, the unfinished railroad embankment in the centre, Pennsylvania College (large building) on the left

statements.quote: which are shown in the background beyond the town
statements.says: Cemetery Hill and Culp's Hill are shown beyond the town in the background (caption continues)

statements.quote: Caption from negative sleeve: Gettysburg from the Cemetery. July 1863.
statements.says: the negative sleeve names the cemetery as the place of view and gives July 1863; which cemetery (Evergreen or the National Cemetery) is not stated

statements.says: camera on Little Round Top, Round Top (Big Round Top) in the distance (title from Milhollen and Mugridge 1977, LOC)

statements.says: camera at entrenchments on Little Round Top, looking at Big Round Top (negative sleeve caption)

statements.says: camera on Little Round Top looking toward Big Round Top (title from item)

statements.says: camera in a wheatfield opposite the Federal extreme left (negative sleeve caption); no coordinates or direction

statements.says: view looking toward the orchard on the Rose farm (title and exact date from Frassanito per the record: lead only, not used as documented)

statements.says: view looking eastward at a line of breastworks (negative sleeve caption); where is not stated

statements.says: the print's own caption describes the clump of woods on the right of the picture as McPherson's Woods where Reynolds was shot; no camera position

statements.ident: caption only: not identified with a catalogued record

statements.quote: Leister B a m viewed from the south and east shortly after the Battle, July, 1863.

statements.ident: caption only: not identified with a catalogued record

statements.quote: Two Brady photographs of Little Round Top, one view from the southwest near Devil's Den and a second view from the northwest at a point near the intersection of the present Wheatfield Road and Crawfor
statements.says: two Brady photographs of Little Round Top: one from the southwest near Devil's Den, one from the northwest near the present intersection of Wheatfield Road and Crawford Avenue
statements.ident: caption only (the report pages reproduce them only as stains: the scan is unreadable)

statements.quote: the view is eastward from the Devil's Den, and most likely depicts
statements.says: O'Sullivan 'View in the Slaughter Pen at the foot of Big Round Top', 6 July 1863: the view is eastward from the Devil's Den; the encircled body lies immediately east of the trolley roadbed
statements.ident: caption only: the report plate is a photocopy and could not be matched; the O'Sullivan "Slaughter pen" record 2018670867 (negative LC-B811-262) is a candidate

statements.quote: The trolley road bed is just to the right of the picture.
statements.says: Gardner no. 265, 6 July 1863, two dead infantrymen in the Slaughter Pen: the trolley road bed (now a path) is just to the right of the picture
statements.ident: stereo number (265 = LC-B811-0265 of record 2018666311; the NPS Then-and-Now image matches cwpb.00901 of the same record)

statements.quote: The area would be just above the present comfort station.
statements.says: Gibson no. 252, 6 July 1863, scene in the woods at the northwestern base of Big Round Top: the area would be just above the present comfort station
statements.match: read from the page image of the saved PDF; the text layer is garbled (not machine-checkable)

statements.quote: modern versions taken from the same location as the originals
statements.says: the NPS states that the modern pictures on its Then-And-Now pages were taken from the same location as the originals (no coordinates given)

statements.quote: This photo was taken near DeTrobriand Avenue.
statements.says: Gardner stereo no. 257 (Confederate dead near the edge of the Rose Woods): the photo was taken near De Trobriand Avenue
statements.ident: image match (1469 inliers) and negative LC-B8184-257 of record 2012647823

statements.quote: This view looks southwest, away from the Rose Woods.
statements.says: Gardner no. 257 looks southwest, away from the Rose Woods

statements.quote: The distinguishing marks on the large rock are still visible today.
statements.says: the large rock in the foreground of no. 257 is identifiable today (reference object, no coordinates)

statements.quote: A large split rock provides a reference point for the location of the original photograph.
statements.says: Gardner no. 235: a large split rock is the reference point for the location of the original photograph

statements.quote: This view faces north.
statements.says: Gardner no. 256 faces north
statements.ident: image match (1411 inliers) and negative LC-B811-0256

statements.quote: The boulder in the foreground and dome shaped boulder in the background provide a reference point for where the camera tripod stood in 1863.
statements.says: two boulders in no. 256 are the reference points for where the camera tripod stood (no coordinates)

statements.quote: the first Then & Now photograph of the same group was taken just a few steps northeast of this photo, facing west.
statements.says: no. 257 was taken a few steps northeast of no. 256, facing west (the NPS caption of no. 257 says southwest)

statements.quote: The modern photograph of this area reveals the Plum Run footbridge and the slope of Little Round Top in the distance.
statements.says: the Slaughter Pen photograph by the pond: the same view today shows the Plum Run footbridge and the slope of Little Round Top in the distance

statements.quote: This staged photograph was taken more than four months after the battle, by Peter Weaver, on November 11, 1863
statements.says: the NPS calls the Weaver Devil's Den photograph of 11 November 1863 staged and more than four months after the battle (not a record of the catalogue: out of scope)

statements.quote: nor is it likely that the soldier fell in this location
statements.says: the NPS says it is not likely the soldier of 'Home of a Rebel Sharpshooter' fell where he lies (staged-photograph flag basis; the body and niche are never used as ground truth)

statements.quote: The body of this soldier would be moved by the photographers from this location to another one some 40 yards away
statements.says: the NPS says the photographers moved the sharpshooter's body some 40 yards (staged-photograph flag basis)

statements.quote: From its summit looking northward, one could see much of Gettysburg, including the Codori farm, Oak Hill, the Brian farm, the “Copse of Trees” and the Wheatfield Road.
statements.says: the NPS Then-And-Now image of the summit of Little Round Top: looking northward from the summit, the Codori farm, Oak Hill, the Brian farm, the Copse of Trees and the Wheatfield Road are in view

statements.quote: A view from Little Round Top today. The Pennsylvania Memorial can be seen in the distance.
statements.says: the modern NPS picture from the same vantage shows the Pennsylvania Memorial in the distance

statements.quote: Natural and manmade fortifications built by Union troops on July 2, 1863 on the southern slope of Little Round Top.
statements.says: the fortifications photograph (three large boulders) was taken on the southern slope of Little Round Top
statements.ident: image match (cwpb.00869 1370 inliers; the Gardner scan 1362)

statements.quote: A photo of Little and Big Round Top, facing southeast. Photographer Matthew Brady can be seen leaning against a tree in the left foreground.
statements.says: the 'Little and Big Round Top from the Valley of Death' photograph faces southeast; Matthew Brady leans against a tree in the left foreground
statements.ident: caption only: the NPS image is not among the catalogued records unless the re-match says otherwise

statements.quote: The monument to Bigelow's Battery can be seen on a rock between the house and the road.
statements.says: in the modern view of the Trostle house the monument to Bigelow's Battery stands on a rock between the house and the road (reference object)

statements.quote: The only sign remaining from the battle is a large hole in the brick gable of the barn left by a cannonball.
statements.says: the Trostle barn photograph shows the barn gable with the cannonball hole (the same wall is visible today)

statements.quote: A photographer’s assistant sits on a fence, looking up at the Lutheran Theological Seminary building.
statements.says: the Seminary photograph is taken from below the building, the assistant sitting on a fence in front of the camera (no coordinates)

statements.says: Brady photographed the Evergreen Cemetery gatehouse about two weeks after the battle (the NPS picture matches record 2018666300)

statements.quote: This modern day picture looks north along the Taneytown Road.
statements.says: the modern picture of the Leister house (Meade's headquarters) looks north along the Taneytown Road; the NPS states that modern pictures are from the same location as the originals
